exposure: Mode of birth (spontaneous vaginal delivery vs. primary cesarean section)
outcome: Mechanical properties of fetal membranes (stiffness, deformability)
Intermediate connective tissue layer fiber alignment
Intermediate connective tissue layer fiber area fraction
cohort: The study participants are fetal membranes collected from term spontaneous vaginal deliveries and primary cesarean sections.
finding: Spontaneously delivered term fetal membranes are softer, easier to deform, show increased water diffusion, and exhibit less ordered and looser fiber structure in their intermediate connective tissue layer compared to those from primary cesarean sections.
mod_finding: Fetal membranes from term spontaneous vaginal deliveries show distinct mechanical and structural changes (softer, increased water diffusion, less ordered/looser fiber structure) compared to those from primary cesarean sections, highlighting the role of the intermediate connective tissue in membrane stability and rupture onset.
cross-section timing: At term, comparing fetal membranes from spontaneous vaginal deliveries and primary cesarean sections.
